lesson.title: Common Words & Grammatical Uses
lesson.subtitle: Everyday compounds, formal patterns, and register
lesson.description: Learn established words containing 以 (yǐ), including 可以 (kěyǐ), 所以 (suǒyǐ), and 以为 (yǐwéi), then explore formal grammatical constructions, lexicalization, and register differences from 用 (yòng).

readings.context: Modern compounds and formal grammatical constructions

intro.lesson_focus: Learn common complete words containing 以 (yǐ), then recognize formal patterns expressing means or taking one thing as another.
intro.core_principle: A character is a writing unit, a morpheme is a meaningful unit, a word is a lexical item, and a construction is a reusable grammatical pattern. Do not conflate them.
intro.learning_priority: Study natural modern words first; formal constructions come second, and Classical Chinese is optional.

overview.core_takeaway: Occurs frequently in established words such as 可以 (kěyǐ), 所以 (suǒyǐ), 以前 (yǐqián), and 以后 (yǐhòu).
overview.independent_usage: Most accessible in established words; independent grammatical use is especially formal or written.
overview.teaching_priority: High for learners of common modern vocabulary.

example.meaning_en: take him as a role model

overview.one_minute_explanation: The character does not map to one English word in every context. It participates in many complete words and some reusable constructions; learn the complete modern words before trying to interpret the character in isolation.

vocabulary.notes: 以为 (yǐwéi) is one lexical verb, not a shortened instance of 以 X 为 Y (yǐ X wéi Y). 可以 (kěyǐ) is likewise an established lexicalized modal; neither provides a freely productive pattern based on historical component meanings.

items.function_en: Using or by a particular means
items.usage_note: Abstract means and manner are frequent; it is not restricted to abstract nouns.

items.function_en: Take or treat X as Y

example.meaning_en: Take him as a role model

items.usage_note: X and Y denote variable constituents, not necessarily single characters.
Keep the fixed element 为主 (wéi zhǔ) distinct from the general slots.
Keep the fixed element 为例 (wéi lì) distinct from the general slots.

constructions.structural_note: The reusable pattern 以 X 为 Y (yǐ X wéi Y) permits variable constituents; 以 X 为主 (yǐ X wéi zhǔ) and 以 X 为例 (yǐ X wéi lì) are recurring subpatterns. The standalone lexicalized verb 以为 (yǐwéi) is a different grammatical unit.

items.title: Asking permission
items.teaching_note: Treat the two-character modal as a single word.

items.title: Explaining a result
items.hanzi: 今天下雨，所以我不出去。
items.pinyin: Jīntiān xià yǔ, suǒyǐ wǒ bù chūqù.
items.english: It's raining today, so I'm not going out.
items.teaching_note: A connective linking reason and result.

items.title: After a time
items.pinyin: Wǒ sān diǎn yǐhòu yǒu shíjiān.
items.teaching_note: The temporal word follows a time expression.

items.title: Talking about the past
items.english: I used to live in Beijing.
items.teaching_note: Marks an earlier period; the present location remains unspecified.

items.title: A potentially wrong assumption
items.pinyin: Wǒ yǐwéi nǐ bù lái le.
items.teaching_note: The assumption commonly turns out wrong in such contexts, but this is not mandatory.

items.title: Formal instructions
items.hanzi: 请以书面形式提交申请。
items.pinyin: Qǐng yǐ shūmiàn xíngshì tíjiāo shēnqǐng.
items.english: Please submit your application in writing.
items.teaching_note: A means or manner prepositional phrase.

items.title: Main focus of a course
items.hanzi: 这门课以口语练习为主。
items.pinyin: Zhè mén kè yǐ kǒuyǔ liànxí wéi zhǔ.
items.english: This course focuses mainly on speaking practice.
items.teaching_note: Recognize the established subpattern as a unit.

items.limitation: Frequently conversational; not freely interchangeable with formal means-constructions.

items.limitation: Especially written/formal in instrumental use; concrete nouns are not categorically excluded.

example.pinyin: Wǒ yǐwéi nǐ bù lái le

items.limitation: That implication is common but not obligatory.

preference_vs_rule.statement: In the instrumental-preposition subset of Sun Dejin’s corpus, abstract nouns followed 以 (yǐ) in 166 of 189 occurrences (about 88%) and 用 (yòng) in 146 of 319 (about 46%). Concrete-noun observations were 23 and 173 respectively. These are corpus-specific collocational preferences, not universal restrictions or contemporary language-wide frequency estimates.

data.sample: instrumental-preposition subset of approximately 2-million-character historical written corpus

items.incorrect_inference: Translate every occurrence of 以 (yǐ) as “using”.
items.correction: Identify the complete word or grammatical construction first.
items.reason: For instance, 所以 (suǒyǐ) is an established conjunction meaning “so; therefore”.

items.incorrect_inference: Apply 可 (kě) + 以 (yǐ) as a productive rule to form new modal verbs.
items.correction: Learn 可以 (kěyǐ) as one word.
items.reason: Historical lexicalization does not create a general productive beginner rule.

items.incorrect_inference: Treat 以为 (yǐwéi) as an unfilled 以 X 为 Y (yǐ X wéi Y) pattern.
items.correction: Differentiate lexicalized words and grammatical constructions.
items.reason: The modern verb is a lexical unit, whereas the pattern is a construction.

items.incorrect_inference: Assume 以为 (yǐwéi) *always* means a mistaken assumption.
items.reason: Often—but not invariably—suggests a contradicted assumption.

items.incorrect_inference: Swap 以 (yǐ) and 用 (yòng) in every sentence.
items.reason: Comparable English glosses do not imply unrestricted interchangeability.

historical.intro: Optional Classical Chinese reference. Pinyin shown is a modern Mandarin reading, not reconstructed ancient pronunciation.

items.function_en: Marks the thing transferred or handled; approximate overlap with some modern 把 (bǎ) constructions.
items.pinyin: Qín yì bù yǐ chéng yǔ Zhào.
items.translation_en: Qin likewise did not give the cities to Zhao.
items.explanation: The phrase 以城 (yǐ chéng) identifies what would be given. The comparison with 把 (bǎ) is restricted to this kind of construction.

historical.caution: Do not treat classical 以 (yǐ) and modern 把 (bǎ) as generally synonymous or freely interchangeable.

questions.prompt: In 我以前住在北京 (Wǒ yǐqián zhù zài Běijīng), does the speaker refer to present or earlier residence?
questions.answer: Earlier residence; current location is unspecified.
questions.explanation: The temporal expression 以前 (yǐqián) points to an earlier period.

questions.prompt: Which sounds natural for casual “eat with chopsticks”?

choices.meaning_en: Unnatural as an everyday conversational phrasing

questions.explanation: 用 (yòng) is the ordinary choice with a concrete tool in this casual context.

questions.prompt: Translate “May I come in?” using 可以 (kěyǐ).
questions.answer: 我可以进去吗？(Wǒ kěyǐ jìnqù ma?)
questions.explanation: The complete modal verb expresses permission.
